explain.say: Big birds like vultures, eagles and storks can stay up for hours without flapping. Their secret is free lift from the air itself: rising columns of warm air called thermals.

explain.say: Sunshine heats the ground, and the air touching it warms, becomes less dense and rises. If that air rises faster than the bird sinks through it, the bird goes up.

explain.say: At the top it sets off on a long, straight glide, slowly losing height, until it finds the next thermal. Hopping from thermal to thermal, storks cross whole continents using very little energy.

faq.a: A thermal is a rising column or bubble of warm air. The sun heats some ground more than other ground, the air above it warms, becomes lighter than the air around it, and floats upwards.
asks: What are thermals in the sky?

faq.q: Why do vultures fly in circles?
faq.a: They circle to stay inside a thermal, which is narrow. Each loop keeps them in the rising air so they climb. Circling vultures are usually gaining height, not always waiting over something that has died.
asks: Why do birds circle in the sky?
Why do eagles circle round and round?

faq.q: How far can soaring birds travel without flapping?
faq.a: Very far. Storks and vultures can cover hundreds of kilometres a day by hopping between thermals. One Andean condor in a study flew for over five hours, covering about 172 kilometres, without flapping.
asks: How long can a condor soar?

faq.q: Why do soaring birds have broad wings with spread tip feathers?
faq.a: Broad wings give plenty of lift at slow speed, so the bird can circle tightly in a narrow thermal. The fanned finger feathers at the tips cut the swirling drag at the wingtip.
asks: Why do eagles have finger-like wing tips?
What wing shape is best for soaring?

faq.q: Why don't soaring birds fly early in the morning?
faq.a: Thermals need the sun to heat the ground, so they are weak early in the morning and at night. Vultures and storks often wait until mid-morning, when strong thermals start, and land before evening.
asks: Why do vultures wait to fly?

facts: Andean condors were recorded flapping for only about 1 percent of their flight time (Williams and colleagues, 2020).
White storks migrating between Europe and Africa funnel across short sea crossings such as the Strait of Gibraltar, because few thermals form over water.
